q: When a substance loses oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is _____.
e: When a substance loses oxygen in a chemical reaction, it is ionised. Ionisation in solution or in the melt produces mobile ions that can carry current.

q: When a substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is _____.
e: When a substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction, it is hydrolysed. A substance loses hydrogen in a chemical reaction.

q: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or _____ element) to a substance.
e: Oxidation is the addition of oxygen (or neutral element) to a substance. Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises oxidation number.

q: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or _____ element) from a substance.
e: Reduction is the removal of oxygen (or electronegative element) from a substance. Reduction is gain of electrons, which lowers oxidation number. Electronegative is the word this version is asking about.

q: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen (or _____ element) from a substance.
e: Oxidation is the removal of hydrogen (or neutral element) from a substance. Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises oxidation number.

q: Reduction is the addition of hydrogen (or _____ element) to a substance.
e: Reduction is the addition of hydrogen (or neutral element) to a substance. Reduction is gain of electrons, which lowers oxidation number.

q: Oxidation is the _____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: Oxidation is the gain of electrons by an element, compound or ion. Oxidation is loss of electrons, which raises oxidation number.

q: Reduction is the _____ of electrons by an element, compound or ion.
e: Reduction is the loss of electrons by an element, compound or ion. Reduction is gain of electrons, which lowers oxidation number.

q: Any element which _____ in oxidation number is said to be oxidised.
e: Any element which remains constant in oxidation number is said to be oxidised. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: Any element which _____ in oxidation number is said to be reduced.
e: Any element which decreases in oxidation number is said to be reduced. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Decreases is the word this version is asking about.

q: In the reaction $N_2(g) + O_2(g) ightarrow 2NO(g)$, nitrogen is _____ because it gains oxygen.
e: In the reaction N_2(g) + O_2(g) ightarrow 2NO(g), nitrogen is oxidised because it gains oxygen. Oxidation is gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, or loss of electrons.

q: When copper(II) oxide reacts with coke at high temperature, copper(II) oxide has been _____ to copper because it loses oxygen.
e: When copper(II) oxide reacts with coke at high temperature, copper(II) oxide has been ionised to copper because it loses oxygen. Ionisation in solution or in the melt produces mobile ions that can carry current.

q: In the reaction $Cl_2(g) + H_2S(g) ightarrow S(s) + 2HCl(g)$, hydrogen sulphide loses hydrogen and it is _____.
e: In the reaction Cl_2(g) + H_2S(g) ightarrow S(s) + 2HCl(g), hydrogen sulphide loses hydrogen and it is oxidised. Oxidation is gain of oxygen, loss of hydrogen, or loss of electrons.

q: In the reaction $H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) ightarrow 2HCl(g)$, chlorine gains hydrogen and it is _____.
e: In the reaction H_2(g) + Cl_2(g) ightarrow 2HCl(g), chlorine gains hydrogen and it is reduced. Gain of hydrogen is reduction in the older oxygen-hydrogen definitions.

q: Oxygen belongs to a class of _____ elements.
e: Oxygen belongs to a class of neutral elements. Oxygen belongs to a class of elements.

q: Hydrogen belongs to a class of _____ elements.
e: Hydrogen belongs to a class of electropositive elements. Hydrogen belongs to a class of elements.

q: In the reaction $Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) ightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$, zinc is _____ due to the loss of two electrons.
e: In the reaction Zn(s) + Cu^2+(aq) ightarrow Zn^2+(aq) + Cu(s), zinc is oxidised due to the loss of two electrons. Zinc is oxidised due to the loss of two electrons.

q: In the reaction $Zn(s) + Cu^{2+}(aq) ightarrow Zn^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$, the copper(II) ion is _____ due to the gain of two electrons.
e: In the reaction Zn(s) + Cu^2+(aq) ightarrow Zn^2+(aq) + Cu(s), the copper(II) ion is neutralised due to the gain of two electrons. The copper(II) ion is neutralised due to the gain of two electrons.

q: In the reaction $P_4 + 5O_2 + 6H_2O ightarrow 4H_3PO_4$, the oxidation number of phosphorus increases from 0 to _____, therefore P has been oxidised.
e: In the reaction P_4 + 5O_2 + 6H_2O ightarrow 4H_3PO_4, the oxidation number of phosphorus increases from 0 to +3, therefore P has been oxidised. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom.

q: In the reaction $P_4 + 5O_2 + 6H_2O ightarrow 4H_3PO_4$, the oxidation number of oxygen is decreased from 0 to _____, therefore oxygen has been reduced.
e: In the reaction P_4 + 5O_2 + 6H_2O ightarrow 4H_3PO_4, the oxidation number of oxygen is decreased from 0 to -2, therefore oxygen has been reduced. For a simple ion the oxidation number equals the charge on the ion. Oxidation number is the charge an atom would have if electrons in each bond were assigned to the more electronegative atom. Oxygen is usually -2, except in peroxides (-1) and in OF2 (+2).
